key_insight: Clinician use of LLM assistants is dominated by documentation and knowledge-retrieval work, but public benchmarks mainly test different tasks, so benchmark scores poorly reflect real-world clinical use.
clinical_relevance: To judge readiness for deployment, clinical AI should be evaluated on the kinds of questions clinicians actually ask rather than on exam-style or curated benchmark items.
method: Analyzed 127,833 queries from 6,342 clinicians across 35 specialties during an 8-month institutional rollout.
Used RCQ-Map, a clinician-validated framework, to label task, intent, answerability, missing information, and potential harm.
Compared real query mix with 58 public benchmarks assembled into the Clinical AI Benchmark Atlas.
evidence_signal: Documentation/administration accounted for 36.2% of real queries, knowledge retrieval 28.9%, diagnosis only 3.7%, and the median benchmark matched just 31% of the real-use task mix.
watch_item: Benchmarks that are popular or designed to resemble clinical practice may still miss major parts of everyday use, so deployment decisions based only on benchmark scores could be misleading.
paper_title: Clinician use of language models diverges from how the models are evaluated
